title: Kiosk Screen Shows the Real School Day | vitalii.no
description:
The kiosk screen in the school hallway showed a bare calendar grid. School events appeared as vague placeholder text, homework lines got cut off mid-word, cancelled lessons still showed up as if nothing had changed, and nobody could tell at a glance which child had gym or swimming that day.

Teachers' messages now rotate across the full lock screen for a whole week, with a view that shows every pupil at once instead of switching one at a time. School events are drawn with a school-building icon and a real, specific title pulled from the source message instead of a generic placeholder. Homework entries are color-coded by subject through a lookup table, and lessons the school marked as cancelled are hidden instead of cluttering the day. PE and swimming days get their own backpack icon pulled straight from each child's weekly timetable.

Long homework text no longer gets truncated — it slides back and forth at its own pace per entry — and extra controls moved onto the camera tile to free up room for all of this. A glance at the hallway kiosk now shows exactly what each child has on today — gym, swimming, homework by subject, and real school events — without anyone needing to tap through menus or guess what a vague label meant.
